explanation: Use cross products rather than slopes, so vertical segments require no division by zero. For nonparallel directions, the two signed cross-product ratios give the position along each segment; both must lie in [0,1]. Parallel segments can intersect only through collinear overlap, where an endpoint of one segment lies on the other. Checking endpoints also handles point segments.
correctness: For nonzero cross(directionA,directionB), solving the two parametric line equations gives unique parameters t and u. The infinite lines meet inside both closed segments exactly when both parameters are in [0,1]; integer numerator/denominator comparisons establish that fact before computing coordinates. If the cross product is zero, the segments are parallel or degenerate. Any common point then implies either coincident point segments or an overlap containing an endpoint. Testing all four endpoints for exact membership in both segments therefore finds an intersection whenever one exists. If no endpoint passes, the parallel/degenerate segments are disjoint. Readonly inputs are never reordered.
walkthrough: Segments [0,0]→[4,4] and [0,4]→[4,0] have t=u=1/2, so return [2,2]. Segments [0,0]→[4,0] and [2,0]→[6,0] overlap: [2,0], [3,0] and [4,0] are all accepted. A point segment [1,1]→[1,1] intersects a diagonal containing [1,1].
timeComplexity: O(1) exact integer comparisons and a constant number of real arithmetic operations.
spaceComplexity: O(1) auxiliary state and at most two returned numbers.
edgeCases: Vertical/horizontal crossings, endpoint touches and reversed directions.
Parallel separated segments, collinear overlap and identical segments.
One or two zero-length segments, nearly parallel lines and coordinate limits.
